title: Claim Submission, Reversal and Cash Re-Bill Deadlines — Prescription Insurance on File
content:
Three calendar-day deadlines of **Prescription Insurance on File** are set per plan class: how long after the date of service a claim may still be submitted, the day by which a paid claim for a fill that was not picked up must be reversed, and how long after a cash fill that fill may still be re-billed to a plan added afterwards.

| Plan class | Timely filing (calendar days from the date of service) | Reversal deadline for an unpicked paid claim (calendar days from the date of service) | Cash re-bill window (calendar days after the cash fill) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | 365 | 10 | 90 |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | 90 | 14 | 30 |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | 90 | 14 | 30 |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | 90 | 14 | 30 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | 90 | 14 | 14 |
| Commercial Copay Plan | 90 | 14 | 14 |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | 365 | 14 | 90 |

## Column definitions

- **Timely filing** — calendar days from the date of service within which a claim may be submitted.
- **Reversal deadline** — calendar days from the date of service by which an unpicked paid claim must be reversed.
- **Cash re-bill window** — calendar days after a cash fill within which it may be re-billed to a newly added plan.

## Comparisons

- The Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit has the shortest reversal deadline, 10 days; every other class allows 14.
- The Medicaid and workers' compensation classes allow 365 days for timely filing and 90 days for a cash re-bill; the Medicare classes allow 90 and 30; the commercial classes allow 90 and 14.
